# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–12 (Complete – Updated 104)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Winter of third year in Mirecombe hill farms; frost on hedges; road rutted and puddled after thaw. Earlier: evening at Brighton following Dobbin's arrival; fine brilliant moonlight night of May, warm and balmy. Army ordered to Belgium before week's end; mobilization imminent from Chatham. Three weeks before French Emperor likely attacks.
- **Primary Locations**: London (Russell Square, Thames Street counting-house, Slaughters' hotel), Brighton (George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Ship Inn, bathing machines on beach), Mirecombe (Seena Orlwood—drowned in flood; Pebin Wexwood, Maric Lindson, Rozek Hollwood, Halan Hollwood, Isbin Hollwood, Orvie, Nynelle Stenworth, Seena Hollett, Brenelle and Orvie Hollett, Thidrek Corrett, Feten Lindner, children of Quenwick, Old Maric), Coldcombe hill farms, Dunholt village (Daric Brackwood, Thivie, Feena Stenworth, Cotho Brackwood, daughter Dalde Brackwood born), Chatham (embarkation point), Belgium (destination), Ghent, Brussels (military balls planned), France (coast visible from Brighton)

## Main Characters

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Role in Marriage**: Primary architect of reconciliation; convinced both to proceed; urged George before Belgium orders; presented gold chain and watch to Amelia; groomsman
- **Confrontation with John Osborne - UNSUCCESSFUL**: Entered City counting-house; received cordial welcome; revealed Belgium deployment; urged reconciliation. Osborne erupted calling Amelia "swindling old bankrupt's daughter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up. Dobbin departed; later sent note to Osborne
- **Brighton Arrival and Actions**: Arrived via Slaughters' hotel; imparted Belgium news to Ensign Stubble; witnessed his tears; dined with officers at theatre box. At Ship Inn: assumed "jovial and rattling manner" to hide feelings upon seeing Amelia; made clumsy compliments
- **In Dobbin's Room with George - COMPLETED**: Delivered lawyer's letter from Mr. Osborne containing disinheritance notice. George erupted in rage, blaming Dobbin; complained about financial ruin. Dobbin replied calmly; offered personal financial support; promised not to forget godson in will. George forgave Dobbin
- **Internal Conflict Intensified**: Deeply troubled by guilt over hastening marriage; feels his own unendurable suspense drove him to crush uncertainty; considers himself traitor to both father and son. Secret adoration of Amelia is now his "greatest privilege and hope of life"; privately resolved he would not have let her go to Belgium if married to her; will not remonstrate with George as master
- **Reputation**: "Greatly respected in the regiment, as the best officer and the cleverest man in it"; backed young Stubble's courage
- **Evening Dinner at Brighton - NEW**: Assumed character of "rattle"; described army in Belgium with accounts of fetes, fashion; described Mrs. Major O'Dowd packing wardrobe with epaulets in tea canister and yellow turban. When Rebecca announced intention to go to Belgium on staff, Dobbin flushed red, objected about danger, became "very confused and silent." Agreed with George and Jos to move party to London next day
- **Knowledge of Amelia's Opinion**: Knows Amelia considers him plain, awkward, ungainly; acquiesces humbly; acknowledges "a time came when she knew him better" but that was distant

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED, DISINHERITED**: Married Amelia late April without father's consent; one week into honeymoon at Brighton; disinherited by father's lawyer letter
- **Financial Ruin - ONGOING**: Receives £2,000 in 4 percent annuities; lost £140 to Rawdon Crawley at cards; must live on captain's pay
- **Military Orders**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; faces "great and certain risk"
- **Behavior at Brighton**: Suffering ennui; eager for others' company; spending time with Rebecca and Rawdon; neglecting Amelia; frequents Rawdon's quarters for cards
- **Response to Amelia's Distress - COMPLETED**: Parried question about foreign service with melancholy; said disinheritance was his concern; gave her letter to read. Upon her cheerful acceptance and quoting "Wapping Old Stairs," praised her resolution; patted her under chin; agreed lady should bear him company to Belgium with Mrs. O'Dowd as chaperone. **Evening Dinner**: Excitement of campaign counteracted depression; applauded Amelia's resolution. Received crumpled family-note from Rawdon asking for money; gave considerable bank-notes and bill on agents. Held council of war with Jos and Dobbin; agreed general move to London next day
- **Departure**: Left Brighton for London by Jos's carriage after breakfast

**Amelia Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED, BRIDE**: Married to George late April; one week into marriage at Brighton during disinheritance crisis
- **Emotional Crisis - DEVELOPING RESILIENCE**: Initially troubled by Rebecca's wit and accomplishments; misgives about Rebecca; observes George suffering ennui; tormented by guilt about forcing marriage and causing disinheritance; blames herself for neglecting mother; views future as "dismal prospect"
- **Response to Disinheritance Letter - TRANSFORMED**: Ran up in alarm; read letter with tender alarm. **Face cleared as she read**; idea of sharing poverty with beloved is far from disagreeable and actually pleasant. Ashamed of feeling happy at indecorous moment
- **Resolution to Go to Belgium - NEW**: Cried with "greatest spirit" determination to accompany George; George applauded, called her "termagant of a wife." Bitterness of parting "juggled away"
- **Departure Preparations - NEW**: Rose early morning; packed little trunks with "greatest alacrity" while George lay in bed; "only too glad" to perform office herself. **Dim uneasy sentiment about Rebecca** filling her mind; although kissed tenderly at parting, possessed jealousy. Left Brighton for London in Jos's carriage
- **Farewell at Brighton - NEW**: Rebecca took "tender leave of Amelia as became two women who loved each other as sisters"; hung on her friend's neck as if parting forever; waved handkerchief out window; Amelia departed in carriage

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Rawdon Crawley; at Brighton; still dunned by creditors; relies on Miss Crawley's relenting
- **Miss Crawley's Door Remains Closed - ONGOING**: Although Rebecca and Rawdon lodge few stones' throw away, old lady's door "pitilessly closed" as heretofore in London. Mrs. Bute Crawley maintains guard: sits beside Miss Crawley in carriage during drives; marches beside her chair during air-taking; when Miss Crawley party meets Rawdon and Rebecca by chance, they pass with "frigid and killing indifference." Rawdon "began to despair" at treatment
- **Monetary Scheme - EXECUTED**: Sent crumpled family-note to Rawdon requesting money from "Cupid" (George) before he departs; Rawdon successfully extracted considerable payment from George in bank-notes and bill on agents. Rebecca remarked to Rawdon: "A comfortable inn in Brighton is better than a spunging-house in Chancery Lane"; noted Mr. Jos and Captain Cupid are better companions than sheriff's officers
- **Intelligence Gathering - ACTIVE**: Through Rawdon's valet who knows Miss Crawley's servants' hall, and by calling in same apothecary attending Miss Crawley (pretending to be unwell), Rebecca obtains information about old lady's movements "pretty well known." Information "tolerably complete"
- **Miss Briggs Reconciliation - NEWLY EXECUTED**: Miss Briggs "not secretly inimical" to Rawdon and wife despite forced hostile attitude. Briggs "naturally of a kindly and forgiving disposition"; now that cause of jealousy removed, her dislike for Rebecca disappeared; remembers Rebecca's "invariable good words and good humour." Briggs and Miss Crawley's household "groaned under tyranny of triumphant Mrs. Bute"
- **Beach Attack Strategy on Briggs - EXECUTED**: Rebecca observed Briggs' bathing schedule; got up very early; brought telescope to bear upon bathing-machines; saw Briggs arrive and enter box; waited on shore as Briggs emerged from caravan. Rebecca wore "kind, tender smile"; held out "pretty white hand." Mrs. Crawley seized Briggs' hand, pressed it to heart, flung arms round her, kissed affectionately, saying "Dear, dear friend!" with "natural feeling." Bathing-woman mollified
- **Conversation with Briggs - COMPLETED**: Briggs saw Rebecca's stratagems "as clearly as possible"; acknowledged Mrs. Bute made match between Rawdon and Rebecca, but Rebecca was "perfectly innocent victim." Expressed fear Miss Crawley's affections "hopelessly estranged" and old lady would never forgive nephew for "imprudent marriage"
- **Rebecca's Assessment and Plans - NEW**: Rebecca "kept up a good heart"; believes if Miss Crawley does not forgive now, she might relent on future day. Notes only "puling, sickly Pitt Crawley" stands between Rawdon and baronetcy; "should anything happen to former, all would be well." Satisfied to have Mrs. Bute's designs exposed and herself well-abused; sees advantage to Rawdon's interest. Left Briggs with "tender demonstrations of regard," assured conversation would be reported to Miss Crawley "before many hours were over"
- **Farewell at Brighton - NEW**: Took tender leave of Amelia as two women who loved each other as sisters; used handkerchief plentifully; hung on friend's neck as if parting forever; waved handkerchief (quite dry) out of window as carriage drove off. Returned to breakfast table; ate prawns with "good deal of appetite, considering her emotion." Explained to Rawdon what occurred with Briggs; made husband share her high hopes
- **Letter Campaign to Miss Crawley - NEWLY INITIATED**: Instructed Rawdon to "sit down at the writing-table and pen me a pretty little letter to Miss Crawley." Rawdon began "Brighton, Thursday" and "My dear Aunt" with great rapidity but imagination failed; mumbled pen-end and looked up in wife's face. Rebecca laughed at his rueful countenance; marched up and down room with hands behind back, dictating letter for him to take down

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER - FINAL ACTION COMPLETED]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Disinheritance - EXECUTED AND COMMUNICATED**: Upon learning George married Amelia, erupted in fury; called George "d---- fool"; denounced Amelia as "swindling old bankrupt's daughter"; accused Dobbin of setting George up. Retreated to study; locked door; retrieved mahogany escritoire containing all George's documents since childhood; examined papers with "curses quivering on livid lips" and "horrid hatred and disappointment"; marked, docketed, catalogued with dates. Commissioned lawyer to draft letter stating determination "final and irrevocable"; George ceases to be member of family; Money expended upon George in minority exceeds entitlement (£2,000 in 4 percent annuities); Mr. Osborne waives all claim upon George's estate. Letter delivered via Mr. Chopper to Dobbin

**Other Characters**: Miss Jane Osborne (learned of marriage from Dobbin; felt violently agitated; defended George; capable of generous forgiveness); Miss Maria Osborne (not displeased; calculated disinheritance might increase her value); Mr. Frederick Bullock (junior partner; man of the world); Ensign Stubble (seventeen years old; purchased new sword upon hearing Belgium news; wrote tearful letter to mamma); Jos Sedley (at Brighton; ordered four horses for carriage to London); Rawdon Crawley (attempted to gain Miss Crawley's favor; passes her with "frigid indifference"; received money from George; sent crumpled note to Rebecca); Mrs. Bute Crawley (maintains guard over Miss Crawley; kept her pitilessly away from Rawdon and Rebecca); Miss Briggs (naturally kindly and forgiving; now reconciled to Rebecca; bathing at Brighton); Mrs. Firkin (Miss Crawley's lady's-maid; groans under Mrs. Bute's tyranny); Ensign Spooney, Mr. Chopper, Mrs. Major O'Dowd, General Tufto, Pitt Crawley (sickly; between Rawdon and baronetcy)

## Critical Facts and Status

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - HONEYMOON ENDING, DEPARTURE IMMINENT**: Married late April; one week into marriage at Brighton when disinheritance letter delivered. John Osborne's determination "final and irrevocable." Upon reading letter, Amelia's face cleared; idea of sharing poverty with beloved is pleasant. George applauded her resolution. Both determined to go to Belgium together. Left Brighton for London in Jos's carriage
- **REBECCA-MISS CRAWLEY RECONCILIATION - NEWLY ACTIVATED**: Successfully reconciled with Miss Briggs on beach after bathing; Briggs assured conversation would reach Miss Crawley within hours. Rebecca's hopes high; initiated letter-writing campaign through Rawdon to Miss Crawley, dictating contents
- **REBECCA'S ASSESSMENT OF INHERITANCE**: Only "puling, sickly Pitt Crawley" stands between Rawdon and baronetcy; "should anything happen to former, all would be well." Views Miss Bute's exposure and her own well-abused reputation as advantage to Rawdon's interests
- **FINANCIAL CRISIS - ACUTE**: George disinherited; must live on captain's pay and £100/year widow's allowance for Amelia; gave substantial payment to Rawdon from bank-notes and bill on agents after receiving crumpled note from Rebecca; lost £140 to Rawdon at cards
- **MILITARY CRISIS URGENT - CAMPAIGN ACTIVATED**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; soldiers facing "great and certain risk." Mrs. Major O'Dowd packing for Belgium; military balls planned at Brussels. Rebecca announced going to Belgium on General Tufto's staff
- **DEPARTURE TO LONDON - COMPLETED**: Council of war held over cigars; agreed general move to London in Jos's carriage with four horses. Party assembled at farewell breakfast; Rebecca and Amelia took tender leave of each other; carriage drove off
- **DOBBIN'S INTERNAL CONFLICT - INTENSIFIED**: Guilt over marriage role unresolved; secret adoration of Amelia now his "greatest privilege and hope of life"; privately resolved to watch and protect her; flushed red and became confused when Rebecca announced going to Belgium
